Search terms for this lesson“how do I build moving platforms and tune jump feel?”Guided build

Today combines two pieces that make the cave fun to traverse: building Platform.cs so moving lifts follow wayPoints and carry the player with SetParent(), and tuning gravityScale + jumpForce with full vertical camera tracking.

Break It Down~10 minGuided build

Move platforms cleanly between waypoints, carry the player with them, and tune jump height across vertical cave shafts.

First, before any code: cut that into parts small enough that you could look each one up on its own.

  1. Step through a List of Transform waypointsStore List<Transform> wayPoints, track int waypoint = 0, check Vector3.Distance(...) < .1, wrap back to 0 at wayPoints.Count, and move smoothly using Vector3.MoveTowards().Read: 4.1 (EnemyController patrol points & List<Transform> index wrapping)
  2. write this partRead: the OnCollisionEnter2D() and OnCollisionExit2D() callbacks in the walkthrough below (CompareTag("Player") + transform.SetParent())
  3. Tag the platform Ground and tune jump weightKeep "Ground" on moving platforms so jumpsRemaining refills when you land, unlock vertical camera follow for vertical shafts, and balance gravityScale against jumpForce.Read: 6.1 & 6.2 (gravityScale, jumpForce, and "Ground" collision tags)

Look closely at Platform.cs: it reuses the exact waypoint-list pattern from EnemyController (4.1) instead of inventing a new movement engine. The new trick is transform.SetParent(), which temporarily attaches the player to the platform so moving sideways does not slide out from under your feet.

Your turn

If Platform did NOT call other.gameObject.transform.SetParent(gameObject.transform) when the player lands on it, what happens when the platform slides sideways?

Look at Platform.cs lines 51-55: OnCollisionExit2D() sets isOn = true (leaving the platform running) and calls SetParent(null). Why MUST it call SetParent(null) when the player jumps off?

In the Editor ~20 min
  1. Open Assets/Scenes/Platformer.unity and place a Platform object (with a solid BoxCollider2D and the Ground tag so jumps refresh on top of it).
  2. Create two or more empty child/waypoint GameObjects (PointA, PointB), drag them to the lift endpoints, and add them in order to Way Points on Platform.
  3. Tick Is On in the Inspector if the lift should move continuously, or leave it unchecked if it should wait until the player steps onto it.
  4. Check Main Camera in Platformer.unity: make sure any Y-axis lock is disabled so the camera follows the player smoothly up tall jumps and vertical lifts.
  5. Select the Player prefab and tune Gravity Scale and Jump Force together (the reference prefab uses gravityScale = 4.5 and jumpForce = 16 — crisp, fast fall with confident reach across gaps).

Socratic: Waypoints, Parenting & Heavy Gravity

  1. If wayPoints is empty (0 elements) when the game starts, what happens on the very first line of Platform.Start()?
  2. Why must the Player have the "Player" tag (matching other.gameObject.CompareTag("Player")) while the platform itself carries "Ground"?
  3. Compare jumping with gravityScale = 1, jumpForce = 7 versus gravityScale = 4.5, jumpForce = 16. Both can reach a similar height — how does the time spent in the air differ?
  4. Why does setting waypoint = 0 inside if (waypoint == wayPoints.Count) work cleanly for 2 waypoints, 3 waypoints, or 5 waypoints without changing code?
In the CodeGuided build

The question this answers“how do I build moving platforms and tune jump feel?”

You are editing Assets/Scripts/Platform.cs. Create Assets/Scripts/Platform.cs (using System.Collections.Generic). Fill in the missing collision parenting line so stepping onto a platform activates it and carries the player cleanly.

This build leaves 1 line for you to write. Everything around it is given, so you always know the shape of what you are producing.

Step 1Declare waypoints, speed, and initial target

Store a List<Transform> wayPoints exposed in the Inspector, a current index waypoint = 0, and public bool isOn = false so platforms can start idle or begin moving when stepped on.

using UnityEngine;
using System.Collections.Generic;

public class Platform : MonoBehaviour
{
    float speed = 2;
    Vector3 waypointPosition;
    public bool isOn = false;
    int waypoint = 0;
    [SerializeField] private List<Transform> wayPoints = new List<Transform>();

    public void Start()
    {
        waypointPosition = wayPoints[waypoint].position;
    }
  1. 1Standard Unity namespace.
  2. 2Gives access to List<Transform> — the same collection namespace EnemyController uses for patrolPoints.
  3. 4Component attached to your Platform prefab.
  4. 6Units per second the platform travels between waypoints.
  5. 7Caches the world position of wayPoints[waypoint] for Vector3.MoveTowards().
  6. 8Starts false (step on the platform to wake it up, or tick Is On true in the Inspector for always-moving lifts).
  7. 9Current destination index inside wayPoints.
  8. 10List of empty child/scene Transforms placed where the platform should travel.
  9. 12Points waypointPosition at element 0 as soon as the scene starts.
  10. 14Initializes the destination so MoveTowards() has a valid target immediately.

Step 2Advance between waypoints and slide smoothly

Inside Update(), advance waypoint whenever distance shrinks under .1, wrap at wayPoints.Count, and move with Vector3.MoveTowards().

    public void Update()
    {
        if (isOn)
        {
            if (Vector3.Distance(transform.position, wayPoints[waypoint].position) < .1)
            {
                waypoint += 1;
                if (waypoint == wayPoints.Count)
                {
                    waypoint = 0;
                }
            }
            waypointPosition = wayPoints[waypoint].position;
        }
        float step = speed * Time.deltaTime;
        transform.position = Vector3.MoveTowards(transform.position, waypointPosition, step);
    }
  1. 1Runs once per frame.
  2. 3Only advances to the next waypoint while active.
  3. 5Arrival check: close enough to switch targets without overshooting.
  4. 7Step to the next waypoint index.
  5. 8Past the end of the list (Count elements means valid indices are 0 through Count - 1).
  6. 10Loops cleanly back to the start of the route.
  7. 13Updates the current target vector.
  8. 15Frame-rate-independent distance slice.
  9. 16Moves smoothly toward waypointPosition by at most step without ever overshooting.

Step 3Attach and detach the Player on collision

Fill in OnCollisionEnter2D() and OnCollisionExit2D() so touching "Player" turns the platform on and parents the player to it — then clears the parent on jump-off.

    void OnCollisionEnter2D(Collision2D other)
    {
        if (other.gameObject.CompareTag("Player"))
        {
            isOn = true;
            other.gameObject.transform.____(____);
        }
    }

    void OnCollisionExit2D(Collision2D other)
    {
        if (other.gameObject.CompareTag("Player"))
        {
            isOn = true;
            other.gameObject.transform.SetParent(null);
        }
    }
}
  1. 1Fires the frame the player lands on the platform.
  2. 3Only react when the colliding object is the player.
  3. 5Starts the lift moving when stepped on.

Check the Platform prefab Tag too: tag it "Ground" so landing on a moving platform resets jumpsRemaining in PlayerController.OnCollisionEnter2D() just like any other cave floor.

// ------------------------------------------------------------------
//  REFERENCE FILE — Assets/Scripts/Platform.cs
//  Written to be read, not pasted. Build it with the walkthrough
//  above, one step at a time, then open this and compare.
//  If it is sitting in your project unchanged, that is the thing
//  to go and do now — the walkthrough is still above you.
// ------------------------------------------------------------------
using UnityEngine;
using System.Collections.Generic;

public class Platform : MonoBehaviour
{
    float speed = 2;
    Transform point;
    Vector3 waypointPosition;
    public bool isOn = false;

    int waypoint = 0;

    [SerializeField] private List<Transform> wayPoints = new List<Transform>();

    public void Start()
    {
        waypointPosition = wayPoints[waypoint].position;
    }

    public void Update()
    {
        if (isOn)
        {
            if (Vector3.Distance(transform.position, wayPoints[waypoint].position) < .1)
            {
                waypoint += 1;
                if (waypoint == wayPoints.Count)
                {
                    waypoint = 0;
                }
            }

            waypointPosition = wayPoints[waypoint].position;
        }

        float step = speed * Time.deltaTime;
        transform.position = Vector3.MoveTowards(transform.position, waypointPosition, step);
    }

    void OnCollisionEnter2D(Collision2D other)
    {
        if (other.gameObject.CompareTag("Player"))
        {
            isOn = true;
            other.gameObject.transform.SetParent(gameObject.transform);
        }
    }

    void OnCollisionExit2D(Collision2D other)
    {
        if (other.gameObject.CompareTag("Player"))
        {
            isOn = true;
            other.gameObject.transform.SetParent(null);
        }
    }
}

Checkpoint — before moving on, you must be able to:

  • Wire a Platform with at least two wayPoints and ride it smoothly without slipping off
  • Tag moving platforms "Ground" so jumping off a moving lift works every time
  • Tune gravityScale and jumpForce together for snappy, readable platforming jumps
  • Confirm Main Camera tracks vertical height cleanly through tall shafts
  • Commit and push
